label: etchcap caps
description: Dense black fungus caps with violet undersides, grown on grain chemistry in the Dark. Rich, mineral and faintly sweet; cooks prize them above any other mushroom.

label: gill-ash
description: A pinch of pale grey-green ash, a few flecks of it still glowing faintly. It sheds from the gill-fans of a gharrek that has fed well on the gusts, and it burns hot and flameless when it is pressed and refined.

label: summ bone
description: Bone from the summ brood's dead: huge, honeycombed and surprisingly light, harder than it has any right to be. It works like timber and holds like stone.

label: summ egg
description: A leathery egg the size of a crate, warm, faintly lit storm-violet from inside. Taken from a summ brood-mother's clutch. Kept away from her, it calls Witchfire storms and a summ comes looking. It will hatch a summing. A summing imprints only where a great bone of its kind stands aboard the ship; otherwise it hatches wild.

label: tholin dust
description: A reddish-brown, faintly oily powder with a greasy sheen: what is left when the Dark's grain has eaten stone or steel. It sweeps up easily, and refines to chemfuel.

label: blue ice
description: A cut block of the oldest ice on the plateau, quarried clean: deep glacial blue shot through with fine white crack-veils, clear enough at the thinnest edge to see a hand through. Distilled-grade water, frozen -- and worth quarrying for exactly that, in a desert with no water anywhere else.

label: blue-ice meltwater
description: A sealed can of meltwater from blue ice: water of distilled purity, with nothing in it at all. In a desert with no water anywhere else, it is worth more than it weighs.

label: char-lace
description: A silver-black lattice of pure carbon, the fused skeleton of a kethevar coil. Light, strong and beautiful, and not a hydrocarbon: it is the one thing from the Blue Desert's flora that is safe to carry somewhere warm.

label: cold wax
description: A waxy hydrocarbon rendered from a Blue Desert native's fuel glands or gut-oil, or harvested straight from its fractal flora. Inert and stable in the cold; store or refine it anywhere warm and it will not stay inert for long.

label: qeshra roe
description: Scarlet glassy beads cut from a qeshra cushion: animal feed for the native grazers, and useless to anything warm-blooded. Inert in the cold; store it anywhere warm and it will not stay inert for long.

label: fexxil glass
description: A sliver of cobalt glass broken off a fexxil burr. Sharp enough to be dangerous in a pocket, and worth carrying anyway.

label: tsevrix pulp
description: Starchy, filling pulp from a tsevrix bladder, sulfur-yellow and sweating condensate. The bladder holds dissolved vent volatiles, so eaten raw it poisons. Roast it at a stove or campfire and the volatiles drive off.

label: roasted tsevrix
description: Tsevrix pulp roasted until the volatiles are gone. Plain, dense and safe: the only plant food in a forest whose meat is all poison.

label: vexxith
description: A sheared vexxith plate, still holding the curve of the animal's flank. Acid beads off it. Fire cannot warm it. The forge-hands say working it is like arguing with something that has already decided -- and everything made from it outlives the argument, the forge, and the smith.

label: zisska meat
description: Dense, dark meat off a zisska, carrying every ring of mineral the animal rasped off the forest's stone. Nobody eats it plain -- a cook works it the way you'd work a fish that could kill you, and the reputation for surviving the dish travels further than the dish itself does.

label: red sap
description: Thick red sap harvested from a sapblister's weeping skin. Not food -- it keeps insects at bay and seals a wound.

label: seed-fist fertilizer
description: An armored seed-fist cut from a bloody fist before it could break off and roll to the burn line to die. Ground down it makes a rich fertilizer. Not food.

label: wombpod sac
description: A translucent sac cut from a wombpod, something part-made turning slowly inside. Left alone it hatches into a bloody mess, the host a genome sample can be injected into.

label: drained fluids
description: Thick, dark body fluid recovered from a drinker's sacks. Whatever it was pulled from, it has been sitting in there for a while. Sealed, it keeps; traders in the dark places know what it is.

label: iridesce chitin
description: A curved plate torn from something that lives at the bottom of the Scald, where the boil gentles to mere heat. Cooled, it is nearly stone; warmed again, it still smells faintly of the mats it grazed. Traders pay for the novelty as much as the material.

label: burst drommath sap
description: A gluttonous payout of sap, all at once, from a drommath burst rather than milked — this animal will never yield again. Worth far more than a season of the trickle it used to give.

label: drommath sap
description: A thin trickle of sugar-sap, drawn off a swelling drommath without pushing it to burst. Renewable, for as long as the animal is left alone.

label: murrelith plumage
description: Flat, translucent ribbon-plumes sheared from a murrelith's tail rather than plucked — they keep their colour and translucency long after the bird has grown a new set. Fetches a real price at market, which is exactly the problem: a colony living off the crown's silence is one bad trade away from a smaller warning.

label: ossagrel sap
description: Sugar-thick syrup wept from ossagrel canes. Distills into a rough liquor or ferments into nectar; the crown's own sap-suckers drink it straight from the plant.

label: potter's clay
description: Grey river clay, bound and lifted clear of the mud by a claithe's own root-plate. Workable straight from the plant.

label: radioactive suppressant charge
description: A sealed charge of processed Uranium, machined to go unstable fast and diffuse into whatever it is dumped into. Foul a Fever Wood pool with one and whatever lives beneath it goes quiet for days — the free-tier answer to a threat the campaign world only ever meets with rarer, more dangerous salvage.

label: giant leaf
description: A giant and very impressive leaf.

label: seep oil
description: Iridescent oil gathered from around a seepril's base. Perfume, lubricant or fuel, depending on who wants it.

label: sekkulaath cream
description: A pale, rich, faintly sweet secretion harvested from a fed captive sekkulaath, thick enough to fill pastry. It spoils quickly, same as any dairy off any animal.

label: sekkulaath spleen chemicals
description: A vial of thick, faintly luminous fluid drained from a captive sekkulaath's spleen. Brewed, it makes a narcotic tea that stains everything it touches purple.

label: severed tentacle flesh
description: A length of thick, rubbery flesh, still faintly warm, cut from a limb of whatever vast thing lives beneath the Fever Wood's pools. It grows back — eventually, on the animal, not in the pack. Traders who know the biome pay well for it; it renders into a rich meat and a strange, purple-tinged tea.

label: thornbug nectar
description: Sweet, thick nectar wept by a calm thornbug — the dairy the arboreal cantons run on. A frightened herd dries up for days; every raid on the guild costs nectar before it costs blood.

label: vaulm lacquer
description: Amber-hard resin, cracked from a sealed vaulm's own shell. It sets glass-smooth and takes a fine finish — a real crafting material, and the reason anyone bothers a defended sap-sucker at all.

label: deep-stratum fossil
description: A heavy dark slab from the oldest layers the canyon walls expose — strata so old they read almost black, holding the edge of something immense: massive plated bone, mineral-dark, still curled the way it fell asleep. Whatever it is, it was already ancient when the flood started cutting this ground. Quest-grade; museum-grade; the kind of find a Farmer keeps quiet about until they've decided who dese

label: fossil impression
description: A hand-sized slab of canyon-wall stone, split to show the pressed print of something that lived and died here in a wetter age — a fern-mat, a shell-bed, a trackway crossing the face. Common enough that every wall near the water line has a few, and worth a modest sum to anyone off-world who has never seen a sky this dry.

label: articulated fossil skeleton
description: A whole small animal, curled in death and caught whole in the stone — every joint still in place after however many thousand floods. Rare enough that a Farmer who finds one tells the story for years, and serious money to anyone building a collection.

label: nabbuq bladder
description: A water-heavy indigo bladder, sweet and crisp. Eaten raw it is a perfectly good vegetable.

label: ruqqal cloth
description: A coarse coral-coloured cloth spun from ruqqal stalks. Rough on the skin and warm for its weight.

label: zennaq filament
description: A bundle of springy verdigris-copper wires pulled from a zennaq. They conduct well enough to bind a coil and are brittle enough to snap at the second bend.

label: raw slime
description: A double handful of the living body, lifted out and still moving. It tastes of warm rainwater and old pennies and it is, technically, food.\n\nIt is also the best medicine anyone has ever found. Whatever is poisoning you — venom, tox buildup, a bad mushroom, industrial runoff — it finds and eats, thoroughly and at once. And then it starts on the rest of you, which is the same appetite and cannot b

label: slime antidote
description: A squat glass ampoule of something deliberately awful: a purgative brewed from the slime itself and cut with enough neutroamine to make it lethal to slime and merely terrible for people. Administered into a converting patient, it kills what is reading them inside a few minutes, at the cost of a day or two of genuine poisoning.\n\nIt cannot help someone already returned to the flow. Before that, at

label: slime block
description: Slime driven through a press until the water is gone and what is left has nowhere to go but hard. It sets pale and slightly translucent, takes a wall load without complaint, and never entirely stops smelling like the place it came from. On a body with no bedrock it is the only stone there is.

label: brakkel fruit
description: Fruit pulled from the dark underside of a brakkel thicket, where it clusters out of sight of anything passing overhead. The Greentide's own foraged staple — richer than a stock berry, and the whole reason nobody in this biome forages for berries any more.

label: dubbol
description: The riverbed is carpeted in filth and sprouts, and this is what eats the filth. A thick, warty, arm-long sweeper of the river floor, moving through the settled muck below the causeways at the pace of a thing that has never been chased. Where the dubbol are thick the water runs clean enough to drink, nearly. Leathery, and it keeps.

label: frenzy dose
description: A single measured dose of refined gorbeleth toxin. Taken, it drives the body into a rising, feverish burst of work — and, eventually, a collapse. Untreated, the collapse kills. Tended during the coma, the colonist keeps whatever the burst bought them and lives.

label: gorbeleth toxin
description: A vial of thick, faintly luminous toxin milked from a gorbeleth's throat sac. Raw, it is only a hazard. Refined, it is the Frenzy's dose.

label: greatbole fruit
description: A single fruit from a greatbole, the size of a person's torso and the deep purple of a healing bruise. It rots quickly once fallen and cannot be carried alongside anything else — one is already an armful.

label: grub spines
description: Stiff, barbed spines stripped from a greatbole grub's arched back. Sharp enough to be dangerous loose in a pocket, and worth enough that people carry them anyway.

label: heartwood
description: A dense, dark-grained timber cut from the living heart of a felled greatbole. It never fully stops growing, even off the tree — a plank of it will slowly warp true again if left alone. Worth real money, for exactly that reason.

label: greatbole seed
description: A single seed from a greatbole fruit. Planted beside open water it grows with startling speed into a young greatbole — and, in centuries no living thing will see out, into an ancient one again. To the Wildsteam Clan, planting one is a sacrament.

label: karrun
description: A flat, wide, root-brown crab-thing that lives in the churnmud between the roots, walking on the same swallowed things the mud hides -- and it finds them. A dropped tool, a lost boot, a coin: the karrun carries it about for a while for reasons of its own. Line-fishers along the causeways pull them up holding things. The claws are the eating; the rest is mud.

label: lozh
description: Lives inside the drowned root causeways, in the channels the roots leave when they rot from within -- an eel the colour of wet bark, thick as a wrist, that hunts along the root-roads at night and ambushes from the same holes travelers step over by day. It is why nobody sleeps with a hand in the water.

label: lunger fry
description: Something young and outsized for its age, no longer than your arm -- which means whatever it grows into is still under this bank. Eat it now, before it eats you next year. Netted rarer than anything else the river gives up, and the one catch every crew brags about.

label: Royal Rind
description: Cured hide off the inside of a greatbole fruit's rind — dense, faintly warm to the touch, and prized across the whole planet. One of Ash'karr's most valuable materials, and the only local protection against the Contagion, the Scald and the Miasma that does not need an expansion to work.

label: saava
description: A wide, thin, freshwater bell that rides the standing fog over the river, half in the water and half in the air, trailing stinging threads a body-length down. Under the fog you cannot see them; you feel them. Not lethal. Memorable.

label: sap resin
description: Thick, amber resin rendered out of green timber over slow heat. Sticky, mildly flammable, and the raw feedstock for anything that needs to be sealed against standing water or hungry ground.

label: sarquin sap
description: Clear sweet sap drained from a sarquin's drip-tentacles. Sugar-rich and mildly intoxicating raw — and the reason sarquin groves are never quiet, so a Jawa tapping one works fast.

label: scaa lumsigh
description: A deep-bodied river fish scaled in green and old gold, with a single seam of cold blue light running nose to tail. It hangs in the slow water under the root causeways and flashes that seam when startled, so a disturbed shoal lights the whole channel for a heartbeat and goes dark. Firm, sweet flesh; the glow fades within an hour of the catch.

label: stellock branch
description: A severed jungle branch whose cut end has drawn itself closed under a glossy amber film. Inside, the pale wood shows its vessels pinched shut in a neat ring, as if the tree had sealed the wound before the branch finished falling.\n\nA doctor or researcher can study it. It rots like any green cutting, in days, so it must be studied in the jungle or carried home quickly.

label: stellock lace
description: A sealed cartridge of stellock film: a fine amber-green lace that, laid over a bleeding person, draws closed across every wound and stump at once and pinches the vessels shut.\n\nIt stops all bleeding for half a day (the length is a mod setting). It does not tend anything: wounds stay untended, still risk infection, and bleed again when the lace lets go. Used once and gone.

label: stench spore extract
description: A reeking green paste rendered out of crushed jungle spore-bladders, harvested straight from a phorrik thicket. Useless as food, and the whole point — nothing wants to be near it.

label: toxin sealant
description: Sap resin cut and cooked with a caustic reagent until it sets into a paste no root, mire or living tissue can push through. Painted over hungry ground it is the difference between a floor and a swallowed floor.

label: tumbel gourd
description: A leathery hollow vessel cut down whole from a tumbel runner. Edible on its own, and worth more to the Jawa as a container than as a meal — the shell keeps its shape long after the plant is gone.

label: tuun
description: A small, quick, bark-mottled octopus that climbs the root causeways out of the water to reach the fruit-fall, and has been seen on the lower boughs. It steals -- lines, bait, small bright things, a fisher's whole catch left on the bank. Rare on the hook because it is usually the one holding the hook. Good eating, if you can find it.

label: uvva
description: A bladder-bodied grazer that hangs under the surface with its mouth open, waiting for the fruit-fall. When the canopy drops its crop the uvva rise in a crowd and gorge -- a fed uvva bloats, spins slowly, and passes seed downstream before it starts again. The river's seed-carrier. Sweet, faintly fizzy, and it does the same to you.

label: vashuu
description: A round, palm-sized river fish the grey-blue of rain on slate, with a dotted line of pale lights along each flank. Vashuu school in the shallows by the hundred and blink their lights together when anything crosses the water above them, so a wading hunter walks through a ripple of blue that runs ahead of every step. Common, mild, and easy to net when the lights give them away.

label: wollick tuber
description: A deep starchy tuber dug from beneath a wollick rosette, the churnmud around it slumping as it comes free. Bulk carbohydrate — the Greentide's honest answer to a hungry colony, no catch attached.

label: yearning fruit
description: Picked off the bush before it could give itself away to something else. Just as sweet, just as loaded with digestive accelerant as the one still hanging — eating it is still free calories with the same tax: fast digestion, a quick return of hunger, and a body that will want to sit down for a minute afterward.

label: zeev
description: A hand-long river squid, green-gold, that lives in the fast clean reaches and moves the way the river does -- one hard pulse and gone. Shoals of them ride the current down through the root causeways and pulse back up at night. Fast to catch, faster to spoil. Its ink is nothing special. Its cousin's is.

label: thump shell
description: An ancient mortar shell with a blunt, padded nose. It barely wounds, but its wide concussion throws everything near the impact - people, animals, loose items - several cells outward. Can be fired from mortars. Explodes when damaged.

label: lanternstone chunk
description: A chunk of lanternstone. Can be cut into usable crystal at a stonecutter's table.

label: crystal carapace
description: A crystallized carapace that is commonly found on arthropods in crystal-heavy caverns.

label: bloodrop moth egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized bloodrop moth egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a bloodrop larva. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: bloodrop moth egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized bloodrop moth egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: gembug egg (fert.)
description: A gembug egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby gembug. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: gembug egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized gembug egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: megapleura egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized megapleura egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby megapleura. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: megapleura egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized megapleura egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: cleaver shards
description: Sharp blue crystal fragments shed by a Cleaver as it fractures its way across the floor.

label: gray shell
description: A strong, gray, chitinous shell.

label: lanternstone
description: Blue native crystal cut out of the Lantern Deeps. It carries light: a block of it glows faintly and never stops. Structurally it behaves like a soft, brittle stone, and it is worth rather more than one.

label: tough chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect. It's quite durable.

label: puffer tendrils
description: Cut tentacles of the twitching puffer. They keep twitching for hours after harvest — pressure, not life — and are good to eat, even raw, if you can watch them.

label: brittle chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect. It is one of the weakest types of chitin.

label: dead venomvine
description: Cane from a venomvine stand smothered until it died - wood that spent its life refusing to burn and, dry at last, burns long and hot. The finest fuel on the plain, and years in the making.

label: fuzz fiber
description: Fine silver-green fronds combed from the fuzz and twisted into loose hanks. Too short and slick to spin into good cloth on its own, but felted with something coarser it makes a dense, light-proof weave.

label: lure fruit
description: A pale, soft fruit as sweet as sugar, grown on a lure venomvine. Anything that eats fruit will cross a field for it. It rots in three days.

label: raw venom
description: Amber venom scraped in thick beads from the canes of an overproducing venomvine stand. Unrefined and dangerous to handle bare-handed; whatever is made from it starts here.

label: pilgrim's token
description: A knot of braided silver-grey wool with a bead or a pebble tied in, left at the foot of a sweetline tree by someone walking the tree-roads. It means nothing to the tree. It means a good deal to whoever left it, and a little to whoever finds it.

label: sweetline felt
description: The coats of every woolly beast that scratches against a sweetline tree, matted and cured in the bark's resin into a dense, soft, silver-grey felt. Warmer than fleece and softer against the skin than anything sheared. A grown tree lets a little go on its own; the rest comes out only when someone strips the bark, under the bark-wardens.

label: vissler arm
description: The shed arm of a vissler: a curled, jointed whip of lichen-grey plates, the ember glow at its joints fading toward the broken end. It keeps twitching for a while after it is cut. Hunters buy them.

label: black insect chitin
description: Hard overlapping scales of insectoid chitin. Exceptionally durable in combat, but a poor defense against weather.

label: dewfringe sprig
description: A handful of dew-beaded fringe, cut from the rim of a shadow. Barely a mouthful of plant matter and the water it carries — nobody farms this, but everybody passing a shade line stops to gather it.

label: bokka egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized bokka egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby bokka. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: bokka egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized bokka egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: gulloth egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized gulloth egg: a leathery canteen of a shell. If all goes well it hatches into a gulloth.

label: gulloth egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized gulloth egg: a leathery canteen of a shell. It can be eaten raw, but it is better cooked, and disgusting either way.

label: pirrik egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized pirrik egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a chick.

label: pirrik egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized pirrik egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: ulgga egg (fert.)
description: Fertilized ulgga egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a ulgga.

label: ulgga egg (unfert.)
description: Unfertilized ulgga egg. Edible raw, much better cooked.

label: gloomcast hide
description: Tanned, dried gloomcast hide. Strong, durable and pricey.

label: gloomcast meat
description: A piece of meat from a gloomcast.

label: mirrak hide
description: Flat, matte, near-black hide that seems to swallow the light that falls on it. Stretched overhead it throws a deeper shade than any other cloth — the predator that imitates shade makes the best shade there is.

label: maidenbloom heart
description: The cream-and-rust heart of a maidenbloom, cut free of its leaves. Rich plant food that keeps for a few weeks.

label: ultriss pulp
description: Pale, faintly sweet pulp cut from an ultriss pad. It bruises fast once out of the ground, but nothing else grows this reliably on open sand nobody else can use.

label: cut ultriss pad
description: A whole pad cut from an ultriss plant, still in its waxy dust-coated rind. Caravans passing through the Long Shade forage these straight off open ground nothing else can use — pale, faintly sweet flesh under a tough skin built to hold what little water it has.

label: vorrel fruit
description: Fat, pale, faintly sweet fruit off a vorrel bush. Split one and the flesh is more seed than flesh. Eaten as it comes it is a death sentence with a few hours on it; put through a proper preparation it is the most sought-after dish on the dayside. There is no third option, and the difference is entirely the cook's.

label: dead crowncarpet
description: A grey, slumped sheet of crowncarpet that died before it reached the press. Worthless as pigment; it exists so a colonist can see what happened to a stack rather than watching it vanish.

label: fresh crowncarpet
description: A folded sheet of freshly harvested crowncarpet, still faintly warm and banded rainbow. It will not keep — it dies of its own accord within a day, and it dies at once if it gets cold. Press it soon.

label: deepfire
description: A jar of pale, faintly glowing pigment pressed from fresh crowncarpet. It carries no colour of its own — mixed into an ordinary dye, it makes whatever colour the dye gives glow, dim and steady, in the dark. Expensive: a whole plant's harvest, refined at real cost, makes only two jars.

label: attar
description: A dark, heavy oil of astonishing scent, rendered from delta silt and salt. Artists brush it over a finished work as a glaze that deepens it; the vain rub it into old scars as a balm. It mends nothing, and it is not medicine.

label: bones
description: Clean bones left when a rotting bed has finished with a body. Light, dry and slightly greasy.

label: delta loam
description: Clean, fertile soil worked loose and cast up by karrobel burrowing through the Miasma's muck. Where the karrobel have been, the ground turns rich and dark — the one export from this biome that arrives already refined.

label: delta salt
description: Grey-white salt scraped from a brelloch's crusted bark. Coarse, faintly bitter and cheap — the Miasma's most abundant harvestable good, and the one the stills need most.

label: delta silt
description: Black, fine and slick silt dug from an immarel bed, extraordinary-smelling and rich with whatever the gradient has carried down. Refines into the delta's luxury attar wherever a still exists to work it.

label: liliana egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized liliana egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a liliana. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: liliana egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized liliana egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: liliana silk
description: Blood-red thread gathered from the liliana, the Miasma's wingless moth, which never stops spinning. Soft, warm and luxurious against the skin.

label: fulgurite
description: Sand fused to glass by a lightning strike, hollow and branching where the bolt burrowed down before the heat gave out. Worthless to sell, satisfying to find.

label: scorch-fruit
description: A fire-cracked seed-pod's contents — sweet, faintly smoky, prized for having been worth the risk. Spoils fast; this was never meant to be stored.

label: furnace hide
description: The banded hide of a furnace-beast, mineral seams and all. It is what the animal used to store a week of deep-dayside sun in, and it has not entirely stopped: a coat of it is warm before you put it on, and stays warm in country that would kill you. In the heat it is exactly as good an idea as wearing a stove. It is also the one leather on this planet that does not particularly want to burn.

label: pyrinth
description: A warm, bright orange crystal. Rare and beautiful. It glows and emits warmth innately which means it can be used to make torches or to heat up rooms.

label: shed curiosity
description: A small bright object left behind on ground where the bolts have been dancing. It is machined - too well machined - and it is not a part of anything anyone can name. Turn it over and the facets do not quite line up the way facets should. Off-world buyers pay well for one and ask no questions, which is its own kind of answer.

label: roach shell plating
description: A curved plate of mechanoid chitin-analogue, stripped from a dead cathedral roach. Its alloy is a minor curiosity to a trader, more interesting for what its patient, tireless owner used to do than for the metal itself.

label: coolant eel
description: A pale, eyeless eel as long as a forearm, cold to the touch long after it leaves the water. Its skin is smooth and faintly metallic, and it goes on twitching for a while after it stops living. Buyers off-plateau pay well for one.

label: dead smartsteel
description: A dense, oddly patterned alloy pulled from the walls of the plateau. It was smart once — self-assembling, self-repairing — and now it is just very good metal, still worth real money to anyone who deals in the strange.

label: live pattern metal
description: Deep under the deck plate, past everything already dug, this metal is not dead. Nothing about the readout explains what it is doing, only that it is still doing it. Whoever pulls it out should be ready for what pulling it out means.

label: captured tetchik
description: A tetchik pinched alive out of its shell-crust. It clicks in the hand. Put it in glass.

label: chatrak plate
description: Scutes cut from a chatrak's back and cured hard. Heavy and unevenly pocked, it will not take dye, but it is the one light-armour leather that turns bullets. Balanced by its weight and by how rarely a chatrak is brought down.

label: cloak lacquer
description: A shimmering film scraped from a chotrix's hide. It bends light. Worked into a cloak at a tailoring bench, it makes the wearer vanish while they stand still and unseen. The effect never wears off.

label: glower crust
description: A scraped-up chunk of black radiotrophic varnish, still faintly warm. Burned, it makes a crude, hot fuel; reduced to ash, it makes a pigment nothing else on the planet can match -- deep, matte black that doesn't fade. Handling too much of it too long is its own kind of story.

label: war dust
description: Fine grey powder swept off the settled film: ground-up munitions, slag and the poison of an old war. Toxic to handle without care. Packs into tox-gas shells, kills blight on a dusted crop, and stretches dye as a grey filler.

label: wreck-lichen scrapings
description: Rust-orange crust scraped off a wreck. Ground and boiled it is a dye base; dry, it burns poorly and smokes.

label: biosilica
description: A handful of clear, glassy lenses cut from a light-pipe nub — real optics, grown rather than ground, and the only non-volcanic natural glass on the planet. Too small and irregular for anything but the most patient hand-fitted work, but genuinely optical-grade: sensor lenses and glazing panels made from it see just as clearly as anything shaped in a furnace.

label: biosilica grit
description: A pinch of silica-cemented crust scraped off the top millimetre of the sand. Worthless alone, but it is the feeder input a patient hand turns into biosilica lenses.

label: brine
description: Salt-bitter water dipped from a cave seep. It cannot be drunk, but a solar still boils the water out of it and leaves the salt behind.

label: crest-plate
description: A curved plate cut from a muurrok's mirror crest. The face is polished so smooth by sand that it throws the sun back like silvered glass. It is light and hard, and it does not tarnish. Set in a ring, a few of them will gather a lot of sunlight into one place.

label: drazzik egg
description: Heavy for its size and cool to the touch, sloshing faintly when moved — everything a canteen-egg should feel like to a hand that has learned to trust that weight. Do not trust this one. Something is already moving inside, and it did not wait for the mother to leave before it started deciding who counts as prey.

label: drazzik egg (unfert.)
description: Heavy for its size and cool to the touch, sloshing faintly when moved. Nothing is going to hatch out of this one — it is exactly what it feels like, a rigid shell of good water.

label: dune crawler
description: A fist-sized, many-legged scavenger with a fused mineral shell, pulled up out of deep sand on a fishing line. It spends its whole life below the surface filtering decayed organics out of the sand — silverbole leaf-fall, dead things the dune swallowed, whatever a wreck sheds — and only ever reaches the light when something eats it or something catches it. Nothing about it says "fish." Cooked, it ea

label: fine sand
description: The finest grains of desert silica, sifted clean and graded small. Traders buy it by the sack: glassmakers want it for high-quality glass, and it has other uses besides. A sun furnace melts it into lens glass.

label: glass pearl
description: A smooth, water-clear nodule fused out of silica deep inside a deep-sand pool — kin to the light-pipe nubs that dot the dune sea's surface, but rounder, and rarer, because nothing usually digs this deep to find one. Desert-world optics traders call a good one "a lens that grew a skin." Sold whole, or cut for what's inside.

label: glass sand
description: Pale, clean drift sand shovelled off a dune field. The grains are almost pure silica, worn round by the wind, with very little clay or iron in them. A sun furnace melts it into plain glass, and a sieve can pull the finest grains out of it.

label: guzzka egg
description: Bigger than a Jawa's own head and heavy enough to need both arms, this is the whole reason anyone braves a guzzka's cavern at all — a rigid shell of good water thick enough to carry a scavenging party home. Sloshing, cool, and not remotely quiet if you hold still and listen: something inside it is already awake, and it did not wait for its mother to leave before it decided you were the reason to h

label: guzzka egg (unfert.)
description: Bigger than a Jawa's own head and heavy enough to need both arms. Nothing is going to hatch out of this one and nothing inside it is listening for you — it is exactly what it feels like: the best drink of water a person could carry out of the deep desert on their own back.

label: ollim wood
description: Wood struck from an ollim stand — bone-white, dense as stone, and grown so slowly that a single plank predates most ruins on the planet. It shrugs off fire and blistering heat the way almost nothing else does, but a hard strike shatters it clean through: the tree traded strength for the one thing that actually kept it alive out here. Prized in a handful of recipes for exactly that trade-off.

label: qorrax egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized qorrax egg. It will take a long time to hatch. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: qorrax egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized qorrax egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: sand sieve
description: A staked driftwood frame strung with fine wire mesh. A colonist who carries one sifts glass sand in the home area into fine sand, a handful of grains at a time, and now and then something harder turns up in the mesh.

label: soorrak egg
description: A rigid, mirror-glazed shell the size of a Jawa's torso, cool to the touch and sloshing when it moves: a full clutch is a caravan's worth of drink. Something inside is slowly growing a sail.

label: soorrak egg (unfert.)
description: A rigid, mirror-glazed shell, heavy with stored water. Nothing will hatch from it; it is exactly the drink of water it feels like.

label: sun glass
description: Thick, clear glass with a faint gold tint, melted out of desert sand by focused sunlight. It is good for glazing, still lids and ornament, and it builds well. It is not clear enough to grind into a lens.

label: aluun
description: A fan-shaped shell-thing that grows on the kelp stems in the light columns, two thin translucent valves held open to whatever falls from the lid, and inside them a mantle that lights — a steady pale gold, the colour of the palette's lamps, bright enough that a kelp tower hung with aluun reads from the shore as a column of small windows. The Compact harvests them by the stem. The meat is a coin of

label: bladderboil
description: A leathery golden sac the size of a head, riding the Scald's boil. When the water around it roars it gulps itself full and swells taut, floating high and hard where nothing else can live; when it drifts into a quiet margin pool it sighs out through its crater-mouths and slumps to a wrinkled bag, half-sunk, resting. Pilgrims call them kettles for the whistle they make letting go. They are entirely

label: cargo float
description: A lattice-timber frame lashed to hoolimbre bladders — load it with whatever needs to go downstream, push it into the channel, and the current does the carrying. A weir catches it intact; even the sink cannot spoil what it holds.

label: doss
description: The eesh's small competitor: a finger-length, hunch-backed shrimp-thing, boiled pink from birth, that works the dung-fall from below where the shoals work it from above — picking over what settles on the mats before the iridai get to it. It is everywhere at the margins in the warm season and it is the pilgrims' snack, gathered with a cloth and eaten from the hand, already cooked like everything he

label: eesh
description: The silver of the Scald. A finger-long, finless, mirror-skinned sliver that lives in the boiling column and feeds on the dung-fall of the herds below — clouds of them, darting, the water's whole budget in a single restless shape. It has no scales; the skin is a heat-mirror, and a shoal turning is a flash you can see from the rim. Netted at the margin it dies instantly and is already cooked, and it

label: ekkel
description: Nobody knows which way up an ekkel goes. A fist-sized knot of stiff, heat-mirror filaments — the eesh's skin grown into a tangle — that lives on the vent walls beside the karrash and rolls: it lets go, tumbles down the chimney in the boil-current flashing like a dropped handful of needles, catches, climbs, and lets go again. It is feeding, somehow, on the mat. Netted it is a ball of hot wire with

label: sealed relic
description: A flask of grown salt, closed all round with no seam anywhere on it, holding something that was alive. The Elder that produced it could describe the contents exactly — the proteins, the trace metals, the isotope ratios, the way the tissue gave up its water — and could not say what the animal was called, where it lived or when it stopped existing, because it has never held those as facts about anyt

label: essarn
description: A finless, bone-white ribbon netted from the Grey Sea's brine — eyeless, salt-rimed, and the one catch here that isn't shy about the open murk. The Grey's most reliable line.

label: fessu
description: A hand-wide, paper-thin fish-thing that is more crystal than flesh: a translucent lattice of frozen hydrocarbon grown around a thread of something alive, flat as a snowflake, drifting edge-on through the fuel where the snow falls thickest. It feeds by growing — each night's fall adds a rim to it, and an old fessu is a plate. Landed it steams in the cold, and it is so light it can be held up to the

label: grusk
description: Blue-black wedges knocked off a pillar face with the mineral foot still attached, so every one comes up wearing a chip of the column it grew on. The meat inside is dark and tastes of the whole sea at once. People are divided.

label: haarn
description: Nobody agrees what a haarn is. It is a jacket of pillar-mineral the size of a helmet, closed all round, that moves — slowly, along the floor, from pillar to pillar, leaving a scrape-line in the silt like a very small version of the giant's. Cut open there is a soft thing inside with no eyes and a great many small hooks, and it dies at once in open air. It is the Grey's only true extremophile: it l

label: heemin
description: A near-transparent sliver hauled off the Chill's top layer, aurora colours still faintly refracting through it before it stiffens in the cold.

label: hessal
description: A bivalve-thing whose two shells are grown from the sea's crystal rather than from anything living, so a hessal bed reads as a patch of frost on the floor. It seals itself for years at a stretch when the brine thickens and reopens when the fog-season thins it, and nobody has seen one open. Prised apart it holds a knot of grey meat that keeps for a week in its own salt and tastes of nothing but the

label: hollu
description: A bell that forms on the underside of the waveglass, up in the ceiling gardens, and lets go — falling slowly down the whole height of the column, pulsing, stinging what it passes, to lie on the floor and be eaten by nuudal. A big garden sheds them all night. Divers learn the fall pattern of their skylight the way farmers learn rain. Netted mid-fall it is a sting and a bell of salt water; cooked, i

label: hydrocarbon flesh
description: Cut wax, spent tar, ripened pitch — the fatty offcuts of the Chill floor's own flora, stacked and inert. Not food, for pawn or animal, on any read of it: a refinery input, full stop, and the fuel chain's very-late-game supplement to the pipes the colony already runs from its ship.

label: iliss
description: A wire-thin eel the length of a forearm, black, with a spine of conductive mineral that the auroral ground currents run through — it lives along the bed of the lake where the electrojet's currents cross, and on a reconnection night the whole floor of a bay hums with them. It hunts nothing; it feeds on the charge, or on what the charge kills. Landed on a wet line it bites with a shock that has knoc

label: immu
description: A finger-long, soft, eyeless fish-thing that lives inside the shells of dead hessal — it never grew any armour of its own and borrows the sea's. Lift a shell and it is there, curled, and it will not leave: shore-folk carry the shell home and shake it out over the pan. It is the most timid thing in the Grey and the only one with any colour, a faint sick pink under the skin. Sweet, small, and mostly

label: karrash
description: Lives on the vent chimneys themselves, in the hottest water anything survives, plated in mineral crust it grows from the brine — a crab-thing that looks like a piece of the vent walked off. It eats the mat where the mat is thickest and is eaten by nothing, because nothing else goes there. Landed, the crust cracks off as it cools and the meat inside is white and sweet. The shells are sold as rim-pi

label: karrud
description: A slab-flat, palm-wide fish-thing that has given up swimming for lying still. The upper face grows a plate of pillar-mineral — the sea builds on anything that holds still long enough, and the karrud holds very still — so from above it is a chip of grey stone with a mouth-slit underneath. It moves only when the brine at the bottom gets too strong even for it, sliding uphill along the pillar bases a

label: kellu
description: The kelp squid: arm-long, forest-dark, hiding in the fronds by day and hunting the shoals in the dark between columns by night. Its ink is the thing — thick, lightfast, black as the Grey. The Compact's charts are drawn in it, and it is the black in every dye-house that trades with the deep. A kellu on the line is half a catch and half an inkwell.

label: kettlewick salt
description: A pinch of crusted white-grey mineral scraped from the collar of a kettlewick, left behind by every clean drop the little distillery ever sweated. Pilgrims of both faiths keep a grain in a pocket and read opposite things in it. Not drinkable, and not meant to be.

label: krellik
description: A crab-thing plated in hydrocarbon frost, each plate a clear crystal grown from the fuel snow and shed and regrown nightly, so a krellik is always half new. It walks the solid propane at the lake's edge and the floor beneath, picking at the crystal flora's fallen fragments, and it is the one thing on the shore the Frostmite will not eat — the shell is too cold even for that. Cracked, the plates ri

label: lamp bladder
description: A fist-sized bladder pulled whole off a hoolimbre stand, still glowing the same soft green it glowed on the plant. It doesn't need clipping to anything or fed anything — set it down and it lights the ground around it until it rots, a few days on, or until you fix it properly to a chain instead.

label: liiru
description: The Twilight's elegant thing: a ribbon-eel as long as an arm and no wider than a finger, that swims upright through the light columns in slow vertical S-curves, and carries along its whole length a single unbroken line of blue-white light. A column with liiru in it looks, from the bank, as if someone had drawn on the water. It eats what falls, it is eaten by the kellu, and it is not fast; it does

label: maalu
description: A bell of grey jelly the size of two hands that has half turned to stone: the sea's crystal grows into it from the rim inward, and a maalu drifts with the weight of its own mineral edge pulling it down, sagging, tilting, never quite sinking. It is not luminous — nothing down here is — and it is not dangerous; it is barely alive. Netted, the crystal rim crumbles and the jelly inside is a mouthful o

label: iridai
description: The iridesce's small cousin: a hand-long, armored, heat-glossed thing that grazes the crowncarpet mats at the margins where the boil gentles, moving along the rainbow bands and taking the pigment into its skin, so an iridai is banded too — a little strip of the Scald's oldest truth. Pilgrims gather them at the baths with a cloth. Cooked the moment it leaves the water, which is to say already.

label: murrol
description: The mud channels' river-fauna made specific: a thick, blunt, near-blind eel that rides the invisible current along the channel banks, mouth open, fat on the nutrient-fed silt, so slow that bank-harvesters pick them up by hand. The deep's comfort food. Nothing about it is difficult, and the Compact's dock kitchens serve nothing else on a bad day.

label: niim
description: The silver of the Twilight — the lit shoal of the light columns, the ordinary fish, the fish that behaves like a fish. Blue-white, hand-long, a dot-line of cold light along the flank, it schools in the light columns under the waveglass in crowds that make the column flash when they turn. The Compact's whole under-lid economy is a net dropped into a niim column. Hunted by the kellu in the dark betw

label: nissik
description: A double handful of glass-bodied pickers strained out of the bottom water, still faintly twitching. Individually they are nothing; by the netful they are the most reliable food this sea gives up, and the shore camps eat them boiled whole, shells and all.

label: noolim
description: A netful of dull silver slivers, hauled up from far under the Twilight Sea's waveglass — never one alone, always a shoal.

label: noothelm bulb
description: A sealed golden bulb harvested off a noothelm stand. Unlit and inert until it is clipped whole to a tether-chain, at which point it wakes and never needs anything again.

label: nuudal
description: The ceiling gardens shed a constant detritus rain from far overhead, and the floor is nuudal: long, soft, mottled, moving through the fall like cattle through a snowfall, eating it. The richest ground in the sea is the mud under a busy skylight, and nuudal are what turn it over. Every net in the columns comes up with a few. Filling, and nobody has ever asked for seconds.

label: oddu
description: Kin to the rime nodule and the reason anyone fishes this shore: a fist-sized shell-thing that sits in the fuel and does what the nodule does on land — draws propane out of its surroundings into a sac of clear jelly that is, eaten, a very mild euphoric. The shell is frost-white and closes when the aurora fades. Raised from the lake it is cold enough to burn, and the scrapers of the Flats carry them

label: oobo
description: Lives in the ceiling gardens, hanging from the underside of the waveglass among the filter-feeders, and hunts by letting go — a soft, wide-armed drop through the whole dark height of the water onto whatever is below, and a long slow climb back up a kelp stem. The gardener tolerates it; the oobo groom the lid's underside as they go. Divers hate it with the specific hatred of people who have had one

label: oomal
description: A blind, arm-long brine-eel the colour of boiled paper, so translucent the salt-crust it has swallowed shows as a grey line down the middle of it. It lives in the silt at the pillar feet and does not come up; the shore-nets take it when the bottom-brine surges. It is always sick — every oomal carries lesions where the salt has got in — and it is never fast. Shore-folk eat it and say it is better t

label: oovanam
description: A soot-dark, flattened crawler dredged off the solid-propane floor, still dusted pale with tholin ash. Uncommon.

label: oovu
description: A bell of frozen hydrocarbon jelly that rides at the surface of the fuel where the snow lands, catching it — a floating cup with a crystal rim, tipping and righting, faintly green under the aurora because the aurora is the only light. It has no sting; it has almost nothing. Netted it is a bell of propane with a frost crust, and the shore-folk keep them for the lamp, not the pot: an oovu on a wire

label: pallu
description: A saucer-sized floater that lives only in the light columns, holding a green symbiont film on its upper skin to the skylight like a face turned to the sun. A bright column is crowded with them, stacked in the water at every depth the light reaches, and a column the gardener lets close goes dark and the pallu sink out of it in a slow rain. The Compact counts them to price a skylight. Thin, green, s

label: pitchpearl beads
description: Glossy black beads, each one a season's worth of the sky's darkest manufacture, rolled and sealed around a grit of ice. Low-grade forage — animals take them readily, pawns only when nothing better is left — and, sealed and portable as they are, exactly what a refinery wants once a colony has one.

label: coarse salt
description: Grey-white salt broken out of the Grey Sea's own formations, still gritty with the sediment it grew in. The commonest substance on a dying sea's floor and the reason anyone dives it at all: the planet's chemical works, made portable a sackful at a time.

label: rime-nodule euphoric
description: A bead of clear jelly drawn out of the fuel itself — propane extracted from its surroundings and left to sit until it is, eaten, a very mild euphoric. Cold enough to burn the tongue coming up, and about the closest thing the nightside offers to a good evening. Tarspool crowns yield the same compound the shore's own rime nodules do; nobody scraping a tarspool crown or cracking a nodule thinks of th

label: saal
description: The bubble-sailor, netted: a bell no bigger than a fist with a single stiff sail-vane that it sets into the trailing lines of boiling bubbles and rides — up the vent columns, drifting down, riding again. The Scald's kindest resident and its signature silhouette; pilgrims read their traffic the way sailors read gulls. Nobody fishes for them on purpose. One in a margin-net is let go more often than

label: sallik
description: A thumb-sized crab-thing that never grew a shell of its own: it excretes the salt it cannot keep out and wears the crust, layer on layer, until it is a walking lump of the sea's own mineral with legs underneath. Touch the water and every sallik within reach pulls its legs in and becomes a pebble. Cracked open there is very little in it, and that little is salt-sweet and good. The crusts are kept b

label: amber crystal salt
description: Honey-coloured salt from the crystals that grow in the chimney fields, carrying whatever the vented brine dissolved out of the rock beneath. Smoky, warm, and the only one of the four that tastes of somewhere rather than of salt.

label: salt cameo
description: A small creature — nobody can say which, or ever could — jacketed whole in pillar-mineral where it sank, the Grey's own statuary shrunk to a fist and made portable. Not carved: grown, the way everything else down there grows. A salt cameo does not rot and does not wear; it is exactly as it was found, and it will still be exactly that in a hundred years.

label: pink crystal salt
description: Shell-coloured salt from the pink crystals, the stain running right through each flake rather than sitting on it. It tastes of iron behind the salt, faintly, and it colours anything it is cooked into.

label: violet crystal salt
description: The rarest of the four, and the one that looks least like it grew. Violet salt comes only from the deep crystals near the pool margins, it comes in small quantities, and it is traded by weight against silver. It tastes sharp and slightly mineral and it is a very long way from anywhere.

label: white crystal salt
description: Salt cleaved off a great crystal along its own planes: flat-faced flakes that catch what little light there is, clean of the sediment that fouls the coarse stuff. It is worth carrying up from the bottom of a sea, which coarse salt is not, and a cook who has used it will not go back.

label: shulla
description: A hot-white sliver netted from between the Scald's vent plumes, a heat-shimmer still playing off its edge as it cools in the pail. Always comes up in company.

label: slackwax timber
description: Cut slackwax, set stone-hard the instant it left the fuel. It holds whatever shape it drowned in — chairs, hafts, window-lattices are all cut straight from a bed of it — and it burns like a torch if brought anywhere near flame.

label: stonewater ice
description: Chipped bone-white ice from a stonewater brake — the hardest mineral this biome owns, granite at −80°. Usable straight from the chip pile for cooking or drinking, cold enough to ache; melted properly it is the only real water the lake floor has.

label: tarnn
description: A colony, not a creature — or a creature that grew like a colony. A branching lattice of clear crystal the size of a bucket, half of it frozen hydrocarbon and half of it something alive threaded through the crystal, growing a hand's width every night from the fuel snow and fracturing back when the aurora is weak. It is the sea's version of the crystal flora on the shore, and nobody has decided whi

label: tarspool stalk
description: A whole tarspool, cut and unresolved: black base, amber middle, violet crown, still banded in the order the sky laid it down. Wicking floss holds the fractions apart until something takes it apart on purpose.

label: tether-chain
description: An alloy-and-bladder chain, the Compact's own showcase work: light enough to haul one-handed, strong enough to hold a cage or a lamp against the current. Nothing in the constellation moves without one clipped to it, and the Compact sells them one or two at a time.

label: thollim
description: Thick grey valves dredged out of the floor sediment, still shut and still heavy. A thollim keeps a fortnight in its own brine without any help, which on a coast with no cold and no rain is most of the reason anybody settles there.

label: shimmer eel
description: An eel that lives under the crowncarpet mats — between the rainbow mat and the rock, in the thin hot film where the mat is thickest — and takes the pigment into its skin the way the iridai does, so a shimmer eel carries dull rainbows down its whole length in the mat's own colours, behind an armored head, and a pilgrim who lifts a mat-edge at the baths sometimes finds one lying there like a strip o

label: tikkarr
description: A long-legged, kelp-coloured crab-thing that lives up in the kelp forest, not on the floor — clinging, cutting, carrying fronds down to its holes. It is the sea-farm's pest and its pollinator both; cut kelp plots without tikkarr in them grow back slow. Armored, a good meal in the legs, and fond of nets.

label: tollhorn core
description: A cut cylinder of soft horn-coral, banded like tree rings: a gold-veined band for every week of standing light above it, a blank one for every dark season. A core sample of the sky. The Compact's well-keeper buys them dearly, and has never once sold one.

label: vaulisk lure organ
description: A fist-sized gland, still faintly gold, pulled from a dead vaulisk. It holds its light exactly as steadily dead as it did alive — no piip, no breathing pulse, nothing a Compact house would ever hang a rafter for. Some things down here keep it anyway, out where nobody has to sleep under it.

label: fallen waveglass pane
description: A whole sheet of the lid, come down entire and settled on the floor — still catching whatever light reaches this deep, still faintly warm from the fall. It will not move again on its own, and it is worth going to: harvest it before something else does.

label: waveglass shard
description: A broken piece of the lid, dense and faintly luminous, cool to the touch even fresh from a fall. It holds light the way the whole sky does, in miniature.

label: weloon
description: A rounded, felt-textured shell netted off the Twilight Sea's floor, a few flakes of the shed waveglass it was picking at still caught in its claspers. Uncommon.

label: zhiil
description: The young of the thing that makes the V-wake. Hand-long, black, ridged, a body built of the same propane-native chemistry as its parent and already agitated by anything that moves in the fuel — a zhiil in a net thrashes until it freezes solid, and then it is a spiny black icicle that thaws back to thrashing on the fire. Scrapers who have fished up a zhiil pull the line and leave, because the paren

label: lamp-black
description: Thick, lightfast ink pressed from a kellu's own sac — black as the Grey, and the only black the Compact trusts for a chart that has to survive salt water and a decade in a tube. Dye-houses on the surface pay for it sight unseen; the deep's own dock kitchens will not touch a squid that hasn't already given its ink up.

label: dhokkur hide
description: Plated hide from a dhokkur, glassy black and heavier than it looks. The boiling rain runs off it without leaving a mark; forge-hands prize it for anything that has to stand between a body and the heat.

label: floatstone
description: A block of floatstone weighs what a lie weighs. Spun glass whirled into tangles, frozen mid-swirl, strong the way a woven thing is strong -- it will not burn, it barely presses on the hand that carries it, and a wall of it looks like swirled stone spun sugar cut into blocks. The Farmers sell it by the promise instead of the weight. Nobody has ever asked for the weight back.

label: ambrosyx shroom
description: A soft, rare shroom. Ambrosyx tastes wonderful and produces a subtle mood-increasing chemical high. However, if eaten too often, it can generate a mild addiction.

label: chitin plating
description: Cured plates of insectoid chitin, layered and bonded for armor. Light, tough, and faintly iridescent.

label: fungal mimic mantis egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized skerrith egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a mantis larvae. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: fungal mimic mantis egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized fungal mimic mantis egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: grellik egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized grellik egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby weevil. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: grellik egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized grellik egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: fragile chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect. It doesn't protect very well.

label: fungal mimic mantis claw
description: A claw from a fungal mimic mantis. It's priceless in most markets. This is a true trophy and needed for special weapons.

label: glimmerslime
description: Glimmerslime is a slime mold, not a real mushroom at all. It lives in symbiosis with the shinecaps.

label: illoth egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized illoth egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a smog larvae. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: illoth egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized illoth egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: orlath cap flesh
description: Freshly cut flesh from an ageless cap, still faintly warm. It has to reach a brewing vessel fast, or it's worthless.

label: lussa crown cap
description: A whole cap cut from a euphoric crown, still faintly luminous. It has to reach a brewing vessel fast, or it's worthless.

label: mirrash veil tissue
description: A cut strip of living veil tissue, still faintly pulsing. It has to reach a brewing vessel fast, or it's worthless.

label: living thurrom hearth
description: A furnace cap taken whole and still alive, warm to hold and slightly damp. Packed into a frame it will keep burning its own tissue for heat until there is nothing left of it.

label: fungal medicine
description: A pack of fungal concoctions extracted from the mortal morel. It is less potent than industrial pharmaceuticals, but much better than nothing.

label: moonless leather
description: Tanned, dried, scraped mushroom layers. A good underground material for making clothes and bags.

label: mushroom leather
description: A squishy damp fabric, not really leather.

label: mushroom log
description: Material from large fibrous fungi. Useful for building structures and weapons. Good animal feed, but largely inedible for humans.\n\nDoes not burn easily and cannot be used as fuel for normal burning but can be used for darklight sources.

label: dulcis
description: Dulcis mushrooms. Nice to eat, even raw, if you like fungus.

label: tough chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect. It's quite durable.

label: brittle chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect. It is one of the weakest types of chitin.

label: mycoid symbiont
description: A dense grey button of gut-wall fungus, bred for a job that has nothing to do with this biome. It is worth what it is worth because of somewhere else — a place where being digested is the local weather.

label: nightwake symbiont
description: A pale, slow-moving thread coiled in a leaf of veil tissue. It wants the base of a skull, and once it has one its host will never sleep again — nor be entirely predictable again either.

label: quickflesh symbiont
description: A palm-sized fold of living tissue, warm and slightly mobile. Swallowed, it finds the underside of the skin and settles in for good, rebuilding damage faster than any human body manages — on an appetite to match.

label: sheenblood symbiont
description: A bead of the Rot's own reproductive tissue, kept alive in a drop of its own sleet. Swallowing it is the formal act of giving up: the Sheen stops treating the host as material. The sun, which the Rot has never met, is a different matter.

label: ageless brew
description: A thin, faintly warm liquor pressed from ageless cap flesh within minutes of cutting it. Drunk fresh, it unpicks years of accumulated damage in a single afternoon — and then the body is saturated, and will take nothing more from it for a year. Nobody has ever managed to carry a cup home.

label: regenerant brew
description: Veil tissue steeped just short of boiling, so the cells survive the cup. For a few days afterward the drinker's body treats every old injury as new work in progress, and finishes it properly.

label: lussa crown brew
description: The crown's cap wrung out over heat into half a cup of something that smells like a remembered summer. It is the most straightforwardly wonderful thing on this planet and it is gone by the day after tomorrow.

label: toxic chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect adapted to toxic environments. It's fairly durable.

label: unjoining draught
description: A vile fungal purge. Drunk, it drives out every living thing joined to the body: muscle parasites, gut worms, any symbiont of the Rot, and anything worse hiding in the flesh. The patient spends a day very sick, and the draught leaves a permanent scar on a liver or kidney.\n\nIf something is hiding in the body that is not a parasite, the draught will find it, and it will come out fighting.

label: bitumen
description: Solid black pitch, rendered from raw tar until it sets hard. Waterproofing, adhesive, torch-fuel, road-metal — half the Sump's economy runs on this one substance in one form or another, and the old paved roads were made from exactly this.

label: dredgel chitin
description: A curved plate off an archive-sifter's back — the janitor's one trade good, taken only if you shoot it, which nobody who wants more digs found ever does.

label: korveth pitch
description: A hard black nodule of concentrated bitumen, harvested from a korveth shrub's swollen branches. Waterproofing, adhesive, torch-fuel — small-scale pitch trade without sinking a dig.

label: tar-cured hide
description: A gulveth's hide, cured waterproof by a lifetime half-sunk in the black. The Sump's own coat — nothing else on the planet sheds tar the way clothing cut from this does.

label: dorvel
description: A fist-sized grey-green barrel harvested from a dorvel plant — bland, dense, and reliable. The reason a Sump colony can eat at all.

label: skelver
description: A waxy, dinner-plate-sized rosette leaf with an oily dark heart, torn from a skelver plant at a pool's edge. Edible raw at the usual penalty — the forage staple of the Sump.

label: seepwax
description: Warm, waxy comb-secretion cracked from a thrummel mound — the hive's own honey-wax analog, worked from tar-sugars by the workers. Nothing about a mound raid is stingy with it.

label: skarrid hide
description: The glass-smooth hide off a still hunter's back — the prize for beating it at its own game of stillness. Cures dark and slick, almost seamless.

label: skellarn spine-chitin
description: The hollow, needle-tipped chitin off a skellarn's stilt-legs — the same spikes that let it stand on the tar. Junkers grind it into awls and fuse-post spikes.

label: strong tar solvent
description: An industrial-strength acid, far past anything the Sump renders for itself — this is the Poison Forest's own line of work, not the tar-country trade the local mounds support. Whatever it touches lets go of tar at once, no scrubbing needed.

label: tar gas
description: Bottled green gas, rendered by working an acid into raw tar until it lets go of its own vapor. The same chemistry the geysers do for free, on demand and by the jug — sharp-smelling, faintly luminous, and the only fuel on the Sump that burns warm instead of foul.

label: tar-ruined goods
description: Whatever this was — food, flesh, hide — the tar did not let go clean. It came up as a single fused black lump, worthless for anything but burning.

label: thrummel chitin
description: Hard, dark plate cracked off a thrummel worker or warden — the under-layer's own building material, tough enough to be worth the mound-raid.

label: thrummel seepwax
description: Warm, waxy secretion harvested from a thrummel mound — the hive's own building material and, rendered right, the feedstock for the Sump's one homegrown acid. A raid on a mound yields it by the barrel; nothing about gathering it is stingy.

label: weak tar solvent
description: Thrummel seepwax rendered down into a mild acid — sharp-smelling, safe enough to handle bare-handed, and the only thing on the Sump that lets go of tar once it has set. A colony that raids the mounds is never really short of it.

label: brine plate
description: A stacked mineral wafer, salt-white and dark by turns, pried off a brineleech that has already spent its charge — or found loose on a pool floor, which is the same thing a season later. It still holds a whisper of charge; touch two together in the dark and they spark. Traders who buy oddities want it.

label: contaminant bezoar
description: A dense fist-sized lump of refined metal-salt contamination, coughed up whole by an excretor animal that spent days walking it out of poisoned ground. Heavy, layered, faintly waxy — worth real money to the right buyer, and worth keeping in small piles only. A kept herd producing these one stone at a time is the closest thing this ground has to a refinery.

label: brineleech
description: The owner. A forearm-long, plated, sea-cucumber-shaped thing whose body is a stack of living electrode wafers, salt-white and mineral-dark by turns, lying on the bed of a hypersaline pool and running on the ion gradient between the brine and the metal beneath it. It discharges as defense. The pool you want to mine has one, and it is a capacitor, and it does not want you there. Landed — carefully,

label: soot brick
description: A compressed brick of fuel-grade soot and ash, pressed out of a sootgrazer that spent the season eating deposition off the flats. Cheap, stackable, burns dirty but burns — and the supply is endless where the sky keeps falling.

label: sparkcrab
description: A salt-white, flat-bodied scraper the size of a thumb, living on the mineral beds under the brine and grazing the crust the brineleech lay down. It carries a charge — a small one; picking one up bare-handed is a tingle and a lesson. They swarm on a carcass in the pool and strip it, and on a brineleech that has spent its charge, which is how the pool's owner eventually dies. Edible after a long soa

label: vitrified bezoar
description: A rarer, larger grade of contaminant bezoar, mined out of a hardened Middenshell corpse's own accreted shell — glassy black-green vitrified mineral fused with metal-salt layers, deep sickly-radiance seams glowing faintly inside the glass. The richest excretor-refining prize in the biome, priced in the dose you take digging it out.

label: clouded piinnok lens
description: A small dome of glass-clear flesh gone milky, now that nothing looks out of it. It is still faintly warm. There is barely a mouthful on it, and nobody who has eaten one recommends it. Fine glass grains are left where the lens was.

label: brimlock water
description: Clear water drained from a cut brimlock bladder-trunk — the only water most travellers in this jungle ever see, since the thicket drank the river whole. Cutting one draws churn regrowth to the spill.

label: ollathrix egg
description: A leathery, bone-white egg the size of a bowling ball, still faintly warm from the clutch it was pulled out of, faintly dusted with silk. Nothing has ever hatched one away from the mother's own nest. Traders who deal in these are not buying livestock — they are buying a very particular, very illegal kind of cargo, and it does not keep for long.

label: quarrok chitin
description: Dull bronze-black plate cracked off a quarrok's slab back, still dusted with silk lint. Tough enough to be worth cutting free.

label: tavrosk liquor
description: Sweet volatile sap tapped from a tavrosk's bole. Drunk straight, traded, or burned in a Wildsteam still — one tapped item doing three jobs.

label: bladder-fruit
description: A fat translucent pod cut from a bladderquill, sloshing with stored water and a little starchy pulp. Food and drink in one object -- where bladderquill stands, nobody dies thirsty.

label: condenser water
description: A litre of clean water drawn out of dry air by the ancient condenser, in a stoppered flask.

label: dewgourd
description: A single melon-sized gourd, rind pale and waxy as the stone it grew in the shade of. Slow to grow, but a colony that has one crop under cultivation eats well for a long season -- the waxy rind keeps it edible long after most produce would have spoiled.

label: dewsilk
description: A pale, weightless fabric spun from mirrik cocoons. It sheds water, stays cool against the skin and insulates well against heat; the Weeping Stones' one export that caravans ask for by name.

label: dewsilk cocoon
description: A damp, pearl-grey cocoon the size of a thumbnail, combed from the mesh wings of a tamed mirrik swarm. Spun at a tailor bench it becomes dewsilk.

label: duul
description: A slow grey sock of a thing that lies on the pool floor and eats what settles -- silt, dung, dead dew-smoke, the ash blown in from the desert. A pool with duul in it stays clear; a pool without them clouds in a season. Every oasis keeper knows the count. It is edible in the sense that most things are.

label: huldu breeding stock
description: A live huldu, picked up and carried home in a wet skin, clinging and warm the whole way. Release into a stocked pool pen.

label: huldu
description: Picked up. It holds on. The easiest catch on the farm, and the one that leaves the handler uneasy.

label: huldu meat
description: Rich and fatty, the winter-feast meat, renders a fine cooking fat (see: rendered huldu fat). It is warm, it clings, it has something like breath, and it was quiet all the way to the kitchen.

label: ikkal
description: A palm-wide bladder that hangs at the surface with a comb of fringe trailing below it, sieving the dew-smoke out of the water as it falls. At dusk the whole pool is dimpled with them, tilted to the same side like cups set out. It has no fight in it; a child can lift one out. Thin eating, and nobody minds -- pilgrims cook them for the broth, which tastes faintly of the stones.

label: ivvol breeding stock
description: A live ivvol, lifted from the floor at night and carried home in a wet skin. Release into a stocked pool pen; a pen is said to run better with one.

label: ivvol
description: Lifted from the floor at night, when the eye-ridge closes. By day it sees the net coming, every time.

label: ivvol meat
description: Dense, mild, good keeping-meat. When finally netted it did not struggle — it went still, and the whole ridge of eyes turned to the farmer, and it watched. Eating the thing that ran your pool better than you did feels like eating the foreman.

label: karrek breeding stock
description: A basket-trapped swarm of live karrek, carried home in a wet skin. Release into a stocked pool pen — bandage before you do.

label: karrek
description: A basket-trapped handful of finger-length armored fish, chitin combs still snapping. Never a line, never bare hands.

label: karrek meat
description: Raw meat from a karrek swarm — individually nothing, rendered by the basketful into a rich paste that keeps (see: karrek paste). Doubt-free, handler-hostile to gather.

label: loomu breeding stock
description: A live loomu, called in with a whistle and carried home in a wet skin, already murmuring back what it heard on the way. Release into a stocked pool pen.

label: loomu
description: It came to the feed whistle. That IS the catch method, and everyone hates it.

label: loomu meat
description: The tenderest meat in the biome, faintly sweet. It learned the whistle, and it answered the whistle, and it was netted with the whistle. Some farms keep one loomu only as the caller for the rest and swear they would never eat that one.

label: murrin breeding stock
description: A handful of live murrin, netted at a wild oasis and carried home in a wet skin. Release into a stocked pool pen to found or reinforce a stock.

label: murrin
description: A hand-length pool fish, deep-keeled, one tall dorsal comb-fin still folding. Gentle in the net and gentle on the plate.

label: murrin meat
description: Raw meat from a murrin, the stocked pool's gentle baseline. Good ordinary fish-flesh.

label: ozhu
description: A blind, comb-gilled eel that lives in the warm throat of the seep itself, down where the spring comes up through the stones. It surfaces at dusk to feed on the fallen dew-smoke and goes back down. Warm to the touch when landed, and it stays warm for a while, which unsettles people. The oldest pools have the longest ozhu; oasis-keepers claim they can taste which spring one came from.

label: seep-salt
description: Mineral-pale salt scraped from the rim of a steamfrond vent, tasting faintly of the underworld it rose from. A preservative and a spice; the only source of it on the planet is a working seep oasis.

label: seep stone
description: A smooth mineral concretion grown drop by drop in the spring throat itself, where the seep comes up through the stones -- the Weeping Stones in miniature, banded pale and dark the same way the cliffs above the pool are. Oasis-keepers set the best ones on the shrine at the water's edge; a lesser one is sold to a pilgrim as a keepsake of the truce.

label: skarrin breeding stock
description: Live skarrin, netted mid-air at a wild oasis, carried home snapping in a wet skin. Release into a stocked pool pen; handle carefully.

label: skarrin
description: A silver arc netted mid-air when the pool is fed — the one catch you make above the water. A missed net is a bite.

label: skarrin meat
description: Raw meat from a skarrin — the volume line, taken at real cost in face-strikes and torn nets. No doubt at all, which is why farmers keep stocking them despite everything.

label: tarrik
description: A thumb-length shrimp-thing with antennae grown into two fine combs that it holds up into the current and licks clean. Kin to the mirrik above the water, and it shows: the same chitin, the same fringed silhouette, the same habit of mist-dancing at dusk, only underwater. It breeds in the shallows during the truce, in the open, in crowds -- which is why nobody who has sat at a pool at dusk can eat o

label: ullo
description: A soft bell the size of two cupped hands, near-invisible by day, that lights a slow blue pulse from dusk. Ullo rise together and drift as a lit crowd while the fan-dancers display on the bank; the pools are places of romance and the ullo have never been told otherwise. Netted, it is a sting and a disappointment -- mostly water, a little meat, and the light goes out in your hands.

label: vhorrin meat
description: An enormous single harvest of rich flesh from a culled vhorrin. The doubt is arithmetic, not flavor: everyone at the feast knows what it grew fat on. See: the Cull Feast.

label: vizhik breeding stock
description: Live vizhik, picked off wet stone after an escape and carried home in a wet skin, gloved. Release into a stocked pool pen.

label: vizhik
description: Picked off wet stone after an escape, gloved — not caught in the pool, caught traveling.

label: vizhik meat
description: Raw meat from a vizhik. Excellent eating, and the pens keep breeding them because they keep arriving on their own. The mild doubt is where it's been — nobody eats a vizhik pulled from the cistern without thinking about the cistern.

label: vobbal
description: Eight soft arms and a bulb of a body, living in the hollows where the seep water enters the pool. It takes things. Pebbles, offerings, a dropped tool, a ring -- and it stacks them, carefully, in towers in the shallows, and knocks them down, and stacks them again. Some oases forbid catching them; most simply don't. The ones who do eat them say it is very good, in a voice that suggests they would ra

label: Kyber Crystal
description: The kyber crystal is a rare force attuned prism that makes up the core of lightsabers and other objects. Kyber Crystals are found when cutting stones into blocks.

label: Bronzium
