description: Considered a cheaper, better-looking alternative to durasteel, bronzium is easier to acquire and work with while still providing adequate protection.

label: Durasteel
description: One of the most common alloys in the galaxy, Durasteel is used for everything from household appliances to military armor.

label: Deathstick
description: Deathsticks are a highly addictive substance common in underworld locales across the galaxy. A luminescent gel contained inside a plastic stick, Deathsticks are smoked as a vapor to deliver intense feelings of relief and painlessness, which some have flippantly likened to the feeling of dying (hence the name "Deathstick"). Deathsticks are created from the brewing of Spice with many common types of

label: Duracrete
description: Concrete infused with steel. Ugly, but tougher than any natural stone type. Required by building codes across the galaxy.

label: Armorweave
description: A thick, protective mesh suitable for tailoring suits of armor with. Though it is somewhat restrictive, it remains the top choice for military outfitters across the galaxy.

label: Beskar
description: Beskar, the purest form of Mandalorian Iron, is one of the strongest materials in the known galaxy. This coveted metal is durable enough to withstand a direct blaster shot and can repel lightsaber strikes with ease. It is a rare and costly substance to produce, and Mandalorian philosophy dictates it should only be used to build the most dangerous weapon in the galaxy: the Mandalorian warrior.

label: Cortosis
description: Cortosis is a metal that has a very high energy absorption rate and transmission coefficients, which allows the energy of a blaster bolt or even a lightsaber strike to be dissipated upon contact. While it has many applications in personnel and starship armor alike, it is primarily used in the shielding of heavier industrial machinery that handles extremely high amounts of energy, such as reactors

label: Plastoid
description: A lightweight yet brittle form of plastic that is highly effective at dispersing energy attacks.

label: Mandalorian Iron
description: Mandalorian Iron is a rare form of iron only known to occur in the Mandalore system. In its impure form Mandalorian Iron is notoriously difficult to work with, but when smelted using secret methods known only to Mandalorians it can be reforged into Beskar, one of the strongest metals in the galaxy. Beskar is notable for its high tolerance to extreme forms of damage, and is durable enough to withst

label: Rhydonium powder
description: Rhydonium is a powdery, highly-explosive fuel substance found on worlds such as Peragus II and Abafar. Officially categorized as a "high-value volatile mote", Rhydonium is one of few substances capable of producing a fusion reaction necessary to power most intergalactic spacecraft, but must first be refined into a liquid state for safe transportation. While unrefined this fuel is highly unstable a

label: spice
description: The most sought-after substance in the galaxy, Spice is in equal measures a powerful narcotic and a powerful healing agent. Large deposits of Spice are only known to be found on Mon Gazza and Kessel, though meager veins of the substance can be found on many other outer rim worlds. The Hutt cartels cornered the galactic market on spice a millennia ago and have since cemented their prominence on the

label: Tibanna gas
description: An exotic, volatile gas that can be superheated and used to generate power or be condensed into high powered energy projectiles. While Tibanna is primarily found in the atmospheres of gas giants, it can also sometimes be found in deep underground pockets on terrestrial worlds.

label: Kolto
description: A rare, extremely potent healing gel refined from a liquid only found in the depths of Manaan. When properly applied (via an instant-use Medpac), it can heal most battlefield injuries in a matter of seconds. Kolto can also be applied directly to a patient's injuries via spray applicator or skilled medical professional, though the quality of wound tending is lower when used in this way compared to

label: Bronzium slag chunk
description: A chunk of Bronzium slag. While it's useless in its current form, it can be smelted to recover Bronzium.

label: Durasteel slag chunk
description: A chunk of Durasteel slag. While it's useless in its current form, it can be smelted to recover Durasteel.

label: Plasteel slag chunk
description: A chunk of Plasteel slag. While it's useless in its current form, it can be smelted to recover Plasteel.

label: water
description: Canned water from a moisture vaporator. A valued commodity on worlds with particularly dry climates.\n\nDUBS BAD HYGIENE COMPATIBILITY: this item will NOT be present in the game if DBH is active. If the "Thirst" mechanic is enabled in the DBH mod options, Moisture Vaporators will spawn DBH water bottles instead of this!

label: ysalamir egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized ysalamir egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: ysalamir egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized ysalamir egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby ysalamir. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: Medpac
description: A Medpac contains essential equipment for the treatment of wounds. They cannot be used by droids.

label: Advanced Medpac
description: An advanced Medpac contains an improved array of equipment for the treatment of wounds. They cannot be used by droids.

label: Antidote kit
description: This kit contains wide-spectrum antidote hypospray injectors designed to neutralize all known poisons and toxic buildup. Damage already suffered must still be healed by other means. They cannot be used by droids.

label: Life Support Pack
description: A life support pack contains dermal regenerators and other equipment for the treatment of wounds. They cannot be used by droids.

label: battle stimulant
description: This stimulant enables the user to better absorb damage and focuses the mind on the fight, improving the ability to hit. The effect wears off after a short time, and side effects are considered minimal. They cannot be used by droids.

label: adrenal stamina
description: A shot of this enhancer provides a temporary boost in the constitution of the user. The effect wears off after a short time, and side effects are considered minimal. They cannot be used by droids.

label: adrenal alacrity
description: A shot of this enhancer provides a temporary boost in the dexterity of the user. The effect wears off after a short time, and side effects are considered minimal. They cannot be used by droids.

label: Echani battle stimulant
description: This stim removes all distractions, allowing the user to focus purely on the battle. The user is almost oblivious to damage suffered. The effect wears off after a short time. They cannot be used by droids.

label: hyper-battle stimulant
description: This stimulant produces a chemical cocktail that sends a boost of adrenaline through the body, focusing the mind and bolstering the user's tolerance for damage. The effect wears off after a short time. They cannot be used by droids.

label: hyper-adrenal stamina
description: Steeling the user against pain, this stim provides a very large boost in constitution. The effect wears off after a short time. They cannot be used by droids.

label: hyper-adrenal alacrity
description: This model of alacrity stim uses a very powerful mixture of chemicals to produce an incredible increase in the dexterity of the user. The effect wears off after a short time. They cannot be used by droids.

label: hyper-adrenal strength
description: More effective than the basic model, this stim uses a risky cocktail of chemicals to boost the strength of the user. The effect wears off after a short time. They cannot be used by droids.

label: adrenal strength
description: A shot of this enhancer provides a temporary boost in the strength of the user. The effect wears off after a short time, and side effects are considered minimal. They cannot be used by droids.

label: bacta
description: A gelatinous, faintly luminous alkali fluid seeded with living bacteria. Immersed in it, a body's own repair goes into overdrive: wounds close in hours instead of weeks, and given enough time even old scarring is eaten away and replaced with sound tissue.\n\nIt is not a medicine you can apply with your hands, and nobody here knows how to culture it. It arrives in sealed canisters on other people's

label: bacta patch
description: A self-adhesive dressing soaked in stabilized bacta gel. Peel it, press it over a fresh wound, and it goes to work immediately — nothing like the tank's slow, total-body immersion, but enough to close one bad cut before it becomes a bigger problem.\n\nIt has nothing to offer an old scar, a missing limb, a damaged brain, or a disease already running its course. It is used once and gone.

label: bacta spray
description: A pressurized canister of atomized bacta, meant to be misted over a whole wounded area rather than pressed onto one cut. It tends and closes every fresh wound it reaches, and its antiseptic base gives a treatable infection a real push toward beating itself — the closest a field item gets to the tank's own reach, in one burst instead of a slow immersion.\n\nStill just a dose: it cannot touch a scar

label: brain worm egg cluster
description: A knuckle of translucent, leathery eggs fused into one lump, the colour of old bone. Something is moving inside them. Geonosian hive broods are laid in the dark of ruins and packed into cargo by people who did not look closely enough at what they were loading.\n\nThey hatch when something warm comes near. They die if they get cold.

label: brain worm egg shell
description: A mortar shell with the explosive filler stripped out and a Geonosian brood packed in its place, cushioned and insulated. It does almost nothing where it lands. Four days later, the people who live there start hearing things.\n\nHurling these at a faction that went to war with you is not a battle tactic. It is a message.

label: marsh fungus
description: A pale, rubbery swamp fungus that grows best in warm rot. Bland and a little sour raw; mashed, it turns into a sweet, creamy paste that hermits on swamp worlds eat like yogurt. Cooks well on a stick, and makes a good starter for anything left to ferment.

label: skewer
description: A pointy stick made from wood. It can be used to skewer and cook food at a campfire.

label: droid head
description: A salvaged droid head, worn from an unspecified faction's service. PLACEHOLDER — the shop/salvage pipeline that drops real faction-specific heads is unbuilt; this generic resource exists so data-spike crafting has something real to consume today.

label: acklay claw
description: The raw claws of an acklay creature. These claws are noted to be quite delicious when eaten cooked.

label: anthropoid meat
description: A piece of meat from a anthropoid creature.

label: bantha meat
description: A piece of meat from a bantha.

label: Baseopsis egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized egg. With enough care and patience, this egg will hatch into a baseopsis.

label: Baseopsis egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized egg. Behind a veil of light the vague shape of a young baseopsis lies curled safely within.

label: crabshell
description: A strong chitinous shell taken from a crustacean.

label: green shell
description: A strong, green, chitinous shell.

label: blue milk
description: Blue milk from a bantha.

label: boneblade
description: Raw boneblade.

label: bufo bile
description: A potent drug procured from the skin of dead gastro toads. It is highly toxic but it gives an incredible high.

label: sentient plant skin
description: Part animal hide, part living plant tissue. Traps cold water inside, acting as a good thermal insulator in hot climates.

label: plant meat
description: A strange meat, part vegetable, part animal, harvested from cactus-hybrid creatures.

label: cameloid meat
description: A piece of meat from a cameloid.

label: cracked ceramic shards
description: What an onnik's gut produces when it was dumped a whole day's clay at once instead of fed in spaced doses - fired too fast, cracked through, and worthless for building or crafting. Good for nothing but the trash heap.

label: crimson silk
description: A blood red silk produced by a species of subterranean moth. It is luxuriously soft.

label: crustapod meat
description: A piece of meat from a crustapod.

label: crystal carapace
description: A crystallized carapace that is commonly found on arthropods in crystal-heavy caverns.

label: deep chitin
description: A nearly inflammable and heat-proof chitin. It is only found on the creatures from the deepest and hottest environments within the UnderRim.

label: Diplocaulus egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized egg. With enough care and patience, this egg will hatch into a diplocaulus.

label: Diplocaulus egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized egg. Behind a veil of light the vague shape of a young diplocaulus lies curled safely within.

label: aaroxis dendoria egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized aaroxis dendoria egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into an aaroxis dendoria larvae. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: aaroxis dendoria egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized aaroxis dendoria egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: acid slug egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized acid slug egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby acid slug. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: acid slug egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized acid slug egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: acklay roe (fert.)
description: Fertilized Acklay egg.

label: acklay roe (unfert.)
description: Unfertilized Acklay egg.

label: basilisk egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized basilisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby basilisk. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: basilisk egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized basilisk egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: beldon egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized beldon egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby beldon. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: beldon egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized beldon egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: blixus roe (fert.)
description: A fertilized blixus egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby blixus. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: blixus roe (unfert.)

label: raw karrask shed

description: A piece of meat from a rodent.

label: ronto meat
description: A piece of meat from a ronto.

label: royal chitin
description: A legendary, royal, chitinous shell. It is only found on the strongest and or rarest creatures from within the bowels of the earth.

label: saurian meat
description: A piece of meat from a saurian.

label: Segnosaurus egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized egg. With enough care and patience, this egg will hatch into a segnosaurus.

label: Segnosaurus egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized egg. Behind a veil of light the vague shape of a young segnosaurus lies curled safely within.

label: silica meat
description: A piece of meat from a silicon based life form.

label: smog moth egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized smog moth egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a smog larvae. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

label: smog moth egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized smog moth egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much, much better cooked.

label: tellurox shell plate
description: A single hexagonal plate cut from a mature tellurox's permanent shell. Unlike a molted carapace, this plate never regrew — the beast wore it for its whole working life, and it shows: dense, weather-scarred, harder than any farmed chitin. The Ascendant Helix bred tellurox for exactly this: an unshedding shell an animal grows into rather than sheds, armor that outlives the beast wearing it.

label: tender meat
description: A piece of tender, fatty meat from a generally sedentary creature.

label: Termitotron egg (fert.)
description: A fertilized egg. With enough care and patience, this egg will hatch into a termitotron.

label: Termitotron egg (unfert.)
description: An unfertilized egg. Behind a veil of light the vague shape of a young termitotron lies curled safely within.

label: tough meat
description: A piece of tough, chewy meat from a generally active creature.

label: toxic chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect adapted to toxic environments. It's fairly durable.

label: brittle chitin
description: Chitin of a giant insect. It is one of the weakest types of chitin.

label: bantha wool
description: Soft, light and provides very good insulation. Wool clothes can keep the body warm even in extreme conditions.

label: coarse wool
description: While somewhat coarse, this wool offers some insulation.

label: nerf wool
description: Soft, light and provides very good insulation. Wool clothes can keep the body warm even in extreme conditions.

label: zakkro egg
description: A single massive egg out of a zakkro's cavern nest, its thick shell packed with cool reserve water rather than yolk — the reason a Jawa will cross open sand for one. Cracked open it drains like a canteen; there is no chick inside to lose, and nothing about it rots or spoils in the shell.

label: giant-wool
description: Long, silver-grey hanks of wool, snagged and shed where the biome's giants have rubbed their flanks raw against a sweetline tree for longer than any settlement nearby has stood. Thick and oily with the animal that grew it — warmer than any sheared fleece, and taken only by whoever is willing to work in the giants' shadow.

label: jawa egg (demo)
description: A demonstration object. Not a thing that exists on Ash'karr, and not part of the campaign: it is here so someone can watch an egg hatch a newborn and prove the engine does what the source says it does. It hatches in a few hours rather than days, because nobody wants to wait for a proof.

label: wrecked cargo section
description: A crumpled cargo section, its hatches burst. Whatever it carried, scavrats and womp rats now nest in what is left.\n\nDeconstruct it for salvage. Until then, ship-vermin keep coming out of it.

label: wrecked hull rib
description: A curved rib of somebody else's hull, torn off on the way down. Mynocks cling to it the way they clung to the ship.\n\nDeconstruct it for salvage. Until then, ship-vermin keep coming out of it.

label: wrecked fuel tank
description: A ruptured fuel tank from a ship that did not make it. It still sweats chemfuel, and the zhakkas that drink it nest in the seams.\n\nDeconstruct it for salvage. Until then, ship-vermin keep coming out of it.

label: fungal soil
description: Rich, dense soil pulled out of the Rot's mycelial mat, still faintly warm and threaded with living hyphae. It keeps metabolizing for a while after it is dug - the bag stays warm on the ride out. Moisture Farmers pay well for it: worked into shade-soil, a little goes a long way.

label: giant ant carapace
description: The hard, chitinous shell of a giant ant. It is exceptionally durable and heat resistant.

label: plasteel slag chunk
description: A chunk of plasteel slag. While it's useless in its current form, it can be smelted to recover plasteel.

label: gravitonium
description: An incredibly durable alloy of uranium, plasteel and gravlite, obtained by compression under large pressure on a grav forge.

label: roach shell plating
description: A curved plate of mechanoid chitin-analogue, stripped from a dead cathedral roach. Its alloy is a minor curiosity to a trader, more interesting for what its patient, tireless owner used to do than for the metal itself.

label: aluun
description: A fan-shaped shell-thing that grows on the kelp stems in the light columns, two thin translucent valves held open to the fall of detritus, and inside them a mantle that lights — a steady pale gold, the colour of the palette's lamps, bright enough that a kelp tower hung with aluun reads from the shore as a column of small windows. The Compact harvests them by the stem. The meat is a coin of sweet w

label: aurora glass
description: A fist of clear hydrocarbon-mineral crystal grown in the lake bed over a very long time, aurora-green when held up and lit from behind — not kyber, and not warm, and not anything a blade could be built from; the resemblance is entirely visual and every dealer on the shore says so before you ask. It is worth having anyway. Frostmites will not touch it and the cold never leaves it, even indoors.

label: bladderboil
description: A leathery golden sac the size of a head, riding the Scald's boil. When the water around it roars it gulps itself full and swells taut, floating high and hard where nothing else can live; when it drifts into a quiet margin pool it sighs out through its crater-mouths and slumps to a wrinkled bag, half-sunk, resting. Pilgrims call them kettles for the whistle they make letting go. They are entirely

label: brine plate
description: A stacked mineral wafer, salt-white and dark by turns, pried off a drazz that has already spent its charge — or found loose on a pool floor, which is the same thing a season later. It still holds a whisper of charge; touch two together in the dark and they spark. Traders who buy oddities want it.

label: crack-wax
description: A pale, waxy lining shed by a Sealed sleeper when it finally wakes and abandons its burrow. Farmers gather it off the flats and line their cisterns with it — the one waterproofing material the Cracked Lands make for free, and the surest sign a dowsing walk found real water.

label: doss
description: The eesh's small competitor: a finger-length, hunch-backed shrimp-thing, boiled pink from birth, that works the dung-fall from below where the shoals work it from above — picking over what settles on the mats before the muddal get to it. It is everywhere at the margins in the warm season and it is the pilgrims' snack, gathered with a cloth and eaten from the hand, already cooked like everything he

label: drazz
description: The owner. A forearm-long, plated, sea-cucumber-shaped thing whose body is a stack of living electrode wafers, salt-white and mineral-dark by turns, lying on the bed of a hypersaline pool and running on the ion gradient between the brine and the metal beneath it. It discharges as defense. The pool you want to mine has one, and it is a capacitor, and it does not want you there. Landed — carefully,

label: dubbol
description: The Greentide is carpeted in filth and sprouts, and this is what eats the filth. A thick, warty, arm-long sweeper of the river floor, moving through the settled muck below the causeways at the pace of a thing that has never been chased. Where the dubbol are thick the water runs clean enough to drink, nearly. The Wildsteam plant them in their channels the way a farmer plants a hedge. Leathery, and

label: duul
description: A slow grey sock of a thing that lies on the pool floor and eats what settles -- silt, dung, dead dew-smoke, the ash blown in from the desert. A pool with duul in it stays clear; a pool without them clouds in a season. Every oasis keeper knows the count. It is edible in the sense that most things are.

label: eesh
description: The silver of the Scald. A finger-long, finless, mirror-skinned sliver that lives in the boiling column and feeds on the dung-fall of the herds below — clouds of them, darting, the water's whole budget in a single restless shape. It has no scales; the skin is a heat-mirror, and a shoal turning is a flash you can see from the rim. Netted at the margin it dies instantly and is already cooked, and it

label: ekkel
description: Nobody knows which way up an ekkel goes. A fist-sized knot of stiff, heat-mirror filaments — the eesh's skin grown into a tangle — that lives on the vent walls beside the karrash and rolls: it lets go, tumbles down the chimney in the boil-current flashing like a dropped handful of needles, catches, climbs, and lets go again. It is feeding, somehow, on the mat. Netted it is a ball of hot wire with

label: fessu
description: A hand-wide, paper-thin fish-thing that is more crystal than flesh: a translucent lattice of frozen hydrocarbon grown around a thread of something alive, flat as a snowflake, drifting edge-on through the fuel where the snow falls thickest. It feeds by growing — each night's fall adds a rim to it, and an old fessu is a plate. Landed it steams in the cold, and it is so light it can be held up to the

label: glower crust
description: A scraped-up chunk of black radiotrophic varnish, still faintly warm. Burned, it makes a crude, hot fuel; reduced to ash, it makes a pigment nothing else on the planet can match — deep, matte black that doesn't fade. Handling too much of it too long is its own kind of story.

label: greenwood
description: Freshly-felled timber from the Greentide's canopy, still damp and heavy with sap. Ordinary lumber once it dries — the real money is in what falls with it.

label: haarn
description: Nobody agrees what a haarn is. It is a jacket of pillar-mineral the size of a helmet, closed all round, that moves — slowly, along the floor, from pillar to pillar, leaving a scrape-line in the silt like a very small version of the giant's. Cut open there is a soft thing inside with no eyes and a great many small hooks, and it dies at once in open air. It is the Grey's only true extremophile: it l

label: heartwood
description: A dense, dark-grained timber cut from the living heart of a Greatbole. It never fully stops growing, even off the tree — a plank of it will slowly warp true again if left alone. Worth real money off-world, for exactly that reason.

label: helixien meat
description: A whole haul of thick, marbled meat off a helixien, the biome's giant. One carcass carries a metal load worth talking about for a year, and a cut of it cooked right is the closest thing this forest has to a feast dish.

label: hessal
description: A bivalve-thing whose two shells are grown from the sea's crystal rather than from anything living, so a hessal bed reads as a patch of frost on the floor. It seals itself for years at a stretch when the brine thickens and reopens when the fog-season thins it, and nobody has seen one open. Prised apart it holds a knot of grey meat that keeps for a week in its own salt and tastes of nothing but the

label: hollu
description: A bell that forms on the underside of the waveglass, up in the ceiling gardens, and lets go — falling slowly down the whole height of the column, pulsing, stinging what it passes, to lie on the floor and be eaten by nuudal. A big garden sheds them all night. Divers learn the fall pattern of their skylight the way farmers learn rain. Netted mid-fall it is a sting and a bell of salt water; cooked, i

label: hurrok
description: A Patient one. A ridged, rubbery, arm-long thing that wedges itself into the seep-cracks where the hidden water is and lies there, year-round, filtering. The shade-line's browsers step over it. It is armored where it faces the canyon and soft where it faces the rock, and it does not come out — you catch one by catching the crack it lives in. Chewy. The name is the sound it makes when pulled.

label: ikkal
description: A palm-wide bladder that hangs at the surface with a comb of fringe trailing below it, sieving the dew-smoke out of the water as it falls. At wind-hour the whole pool is dimpled with them, tilted to the same side like cups set out. It has no fight in it; a child can lift one out. Thin eating, and nobody minds -- pilgrims cook them for the broth, which tastes faintly of the stones.

label: iliss
description: A wire-thin eel the length of a forearm, black, with a spine of conductive mineral that the auroral ground currents run through — it lives along the bed of the lake where the electrojet's currents cross, and on a reconnection night the whole floor of a bay hums with them. It hunts nothing; it feeds on the charge, or on what the charge kills. Landed on a wet line it bites with a shock that has knoc

label: immu
description: A finger-long, soft, eyeless fish-thing that lives inside the shells of dead hessal — it never grew any armour of its own and borrows the sea's. Lift a shell and it is there, curled, and it will not leave: shore-folk carry the shell home and shake it out over the pan. It is the most timid thing in the Grey and the only one with any colour, a faint sick pink under the skin. Sweet, small, and mostly

label: karrash
description: Lives on the vent chimneys themselves, in the hottest water anything survives, plated in mineral crust it grows from the brine — a crab-thing that looks like a piece of the vent walked off. It eats the mat where the mat is thickest and is eaten by nothing, because nothing else goes there. Landed, the crust cracks off as it cools and the meat inside is white and sweet. The shells are sold as rim-pi

label: karrud
description: A slab-flat, palm-wide fish-thing that has given up swimming for lying still. The upper face grows a plate of pillar-mineral — the sea builds on anything that holds still long enough, and the karrud holds very still — so from above it is a chip of grey stone with a mouth-slit underneath. It moves only when the brine at the bottom gets too strong even for it, sliding uphill along the pillar bases a

label: karrun
description: A flat, wide, root-brown crab-thing that lives in the churnmud between the giants, walking on the same swallowed things the mud hides -- and it finds them. A dropped tool, a lost boot, a coin: the karrun carries it about for a while for reasons of its own. Line-fishers along the causeways pull them up holding things. The claws are the eating; the rest is mud.

label: kellu
description: The kelp squid: arm-long, forest-dark, hiding in the fronds by day and hunting the shoals in the dark between columns by night. Its ink is the thing — thick, lightfast, black as the Grey. The Compact's charts are drawn in it, and it is the black in every dye-house that trades with the deep. A kellu on the line is half a catch and half an inkwell.

label: krellik
description: A crab-thing plated in hydrocarbon frost, each plate a clear crystal grown from the fuel snow and shed and regrown nightly, so a krellik is always half new. It walks the solid propane at the lake's edge and the floor beneath, picking at the crystal flora's fallen fragments, and it is the one thing on the shore the Frostmite will not eat — the shell is too cold even for that. Cracked, the plates ri

label: liiru
description: The Twilight's elegant thing: a ribbon-eel as long as an arm and no wider than a finger, that swims upright through the light columns in slow vertical S-curves, and carries along its whole length a single unbroken line of blue-white light. A column with liiru in it looks, from the bank, as if someone had drawn on the water. It eats what falls, it is eaten by the kellu, and it is not fast; it does

label: lozh
description: Lives inside the drowned root causeways, in the channels the roots leave when they rot from within -- an eel the colour of wet bark, thick as a wrist, that hunts along the root-roads at night and ambushes from the same holes travelers step over by day. It is why the causeways are contested by everything that prefers dry footing, and why nobody sleeps with a hand in the water.

label: lunger fry
description: A Lunger no longer than your arm, which means its mother is under this bank -- eat it now, before it eats you next year. The Greentide's one prize fish: netted rarer than anything else the river gives up, and the one catch every Wildsteam crew brags about.

label: maalu
description: A bell of grey jelly the size of two hands that has half turned to stone: the sea's crystal grows into it from the rim inward, and a maalu drifts with the weight of its own mineral edge pulling it down, sagging, tilting, never quite sinking. It is not luminous — nothing down here is — and it is not dangerous; it is barely alive. Netted, the crystal rim crumbles and the jelly inside is a mouthful o

label: metal-salt bezoar
description: A dense, layered pellet an excretor sheds once it has concentrated all the contamination its body can hold — mineral salts and heavy metals packed into a hard, handleable lump. A kept herd hands these back on a schedule, which is as close to refining as grazing gets: they extract the poison, they never destroy it, and the pellet still has to go somewhere once you have it.

label: mindstone
description: A fist-sized crystal, smooth as a river pebble, with a pale light deep inside it that never flickers. The miners' word for it is mindstone. Speak near it and it hums a half-beat after you, never with you, as if it were learning the shape of your voice. Droids do not like to be near it.

label: muddal
description: The bottom-walkers' small cousin: a hand-long, armored, heat-glossed thing that grazes the crowncarpet mats at the margins where the boil gentles, moving along the rainbow bands and taking the pigment into its skin, so a muddal is banded too — a little strip of the Scald's oldest truth. Pilgrims gather them at the baths with a cloth. Cooked the moment it leaves the water, which is to say already.

label: murrol
description: The mud channels' river-fauna made specific: a thick, blunt, near-blind eel that rides the invisible current along the channel banks, mouth open, fat on the nutrient-fed silt, so slow that bank-harvesters pick them up by hand. The deep's comfort food. Nothing about it is difficult, and the Compact's dock kitchens serve nothing else on a bad day.

label: neebray meat
description: Thin, silica-veined meat off a neebray, carrying the same metal-rich tailings the whole biome sweats out. Nobody eats it plain — a cook works it the way you'd work a fish that could kill you, and the reputation for surviving the dish travels further than the dish itself does.

label: niim
description: The silver of the Twilight — the shoal fish, the ordinary fish, the fish that behaves like a fish, and the only one on the planet that does. Blue-white, hand-long, a dot-line of cold light along the flank, it schools in the light columns under the waveglass in crowds that make the column flash when they turn. The Compact's whole under-lid economy is a net dropped into a niim column. Hunted by the

label: nuudal
description: The ceiling gardens shed a constant detritus rain, and the floor is nuudal: long, soft, mottled, moving through the fall like cattle through a snowfall, eating it. The richest ground in the sea is the mud under a busy skylight, and nuudal are what turn it over. Every net in the columns comes up with a few. Filling, and nobody has ever asked for seconds.

label: oddu
description: Kin to the rime nodule and the reason anyone fishes this shore: a fist-sized shell-thing that sits in the fuel and does what the nodule does on land — draws propane out of its surroundings into a sac of clear jelly that is, eaten, a very mild euphoric. The shell is frost-white and closes when the aurora fades. Raised from the lake it is cold enough to burn, and the scrapers of the Flats carry them

label: oobo
description: Lives in the ceiling gardens, hanging from the underside of the waveglass among the filter-feeders, and hunts by letting go — a soft, wide-armed drop through the whole dark height of the water onto whatever is below, and a long slow climb back up a kelp stem. The gardener tolerates it; the oobo groom the lid's underside as they go. Divers hate it with the specific hatred of people who have had one

label: oomal
description: A blind, arm-long brine-eel the colour of boiled paper, so translucent the salt-crust it has swallowed shows as a grey line down the middle of it. It lives in the silt at the pillar feet and does not come up; the shore-nets take it when the bottom-brine surges. It is always sick — every oomal carries lesions where the salt has got in — and it is never fast. Shore-folk eat it and say it is better t

label: oovu
description: A bell of frozen hydrocarbon jelly that rides at the surface of the fuel where the snow lands, catching it — a floating cup with a crystal rim, tipping and righting, faintly green under the aurora because the aurora is the only light. It has no sting; it has almost nothing. Netted it is a bell of propane with a frost crust, and the shore-folk keep them for the lamp, not the pot: an oovu on a wire

label: ozhu
description: A blind, comb-gilled eel that lives in the warm throat of the seep itself, down where the spring comes up through the stones. It surfaces at wind-hour to feed on the fallen dew-smoke and goes back down. Warm to the touch when landed, and it stays warm for a while, which unsettles people. The oldest pools have the longest ozhu; oasis-keepers claim they can taste which spring one came from.

label: pallu
description: A saucer-sized floater that lives only in the light columns, holding a green symbiont film on its upper skin to the skylight like a face turned to the sun. A bright column is crowded with them, stacked in the water at every depth the light reaches, and a column the gardener lets close goes dark and the pallu sink out of it in a slow rain. The Compact counts them to price a skylight. Thin, green, s

label: giant leaf
description: A giant and very impressive leaf.

label: saal
description: The bubble-sailor, netted: a bell no bigger than a fist with a single stiff sail-vane that it sets into the trailing lines of boiling bubbles and rides — up the vent columns, drifting down, riding again. The Scald's kindest resident and its signature silhouette; pilgrims read their traffic the way sailors read gulls. Nobody fishes for them on purpose. One in a margin-net is let go more often than

label: saava
description: A wide, thin, freshwater bell that rides the Roil -- the steam-fog over the river -- half in the water and half in the air, trailing stinging threads a body-length down. Under the fog you cannot see them; you feel them. Not lethal. Memorable. A dozen drying on a line is a Wildsteam camp's fly-screen.

label: sallik
description: A thumb-sized crab-thing that never grew a shell of its own: it excretes the salt it cannot keep out and wears the crust, layer on layer, until it is a walking lump of the sea's own mineral with legs underneath. Touch the water and every sallik within reach pulls its legs in and becomes a pebble. Cracked open there is very little in it, and that little is salt-sweet and good. The crusts are kept b

label: salt cameo
description: A small creature — nobody can say which, or ever could — jacketed whole in pillar-mineral where it sank, the Grey's own statuary shrunk to a fist and made portable. Not carved: grown, the way everything else down there grows. A salt cameo does not rot and does not wear; it is exactly as it was found, and it will still be exactly that in a hundred years.

label: screecher meat
description: Dark, stringy meat off a poison forest screecher, still faintly acrid from whatever it last stunned and ate. The toxin is real; so is the reputation the dish carries when it's cooked right.

label: sealed water jar
description: A clay jar, waxed shut, still full. Water kept for the Return and never poured. Pour it into the sand to pay the Debt.

label: seep stone
description: A smooth mineral concretion grown drop by drop in the spring throat itself, where the seep comes up through the stones -- the Weeping Stones in miniature, banded pale and dark the same way the cliffs above the pool are. Oasis-keepers set the best ones on the shrine at the water's edge; a lesser one is sold to a pilgrim as a keepsake of the truce.

label: tarnn
description: A colony, not a creature — or a creature that grew like a colony. A branching lattice of clear crystal the size of a bucket, half of it frozen hydrocarbon and half of it something alive threaded through the crystal, growing a hand's width every night from the fuel snow and fracturing back when the aurora is weak. It is the sea's version of the crystal flora on the shore, and nobody has decided whi

label: tarrik
description: A thumb-length shrimp-thing with antennae grown into two fine combs that it holds up into the current and licks clean. Kin to the mirrik above the water, and it shows: the same chitin, the same fringed silhouette, the same habit of mist-dancing at wind-hour, only underwater. It breeds in the shallows during the truce, in the open, in crowds -- which is why nobody who has sat at a pool at dusk can

label: tekk
description: A salt-white, flat-bodied scraper the size of a thumb, living on the mineral beds under the brine and grazing the crust the drazz lay down. It carries a charge — a small one; picking one up bare-handed is a tingle and a lesson. They swarm on a carcass in the pool and strip it, and on a drazz that has spent its charge, which is how the pool's owner eventually dies. Edible after a long soak. The Jun

label: thuum
description: An eel that lives under the crowncarpet mats — between the rainbow mat and the rock, in the thin hot film where the mat is thickest — and takes the pigment into its skin the way the muddal does, so a thuum is banded down its whole length in the mat's own colours, and a pilgrim who lifts a mat-edge at the baths sometimes finds one lying there like a strip of the Scald's oldest truth that has learne

label: tibanna gas
description: Pressurized gas tapped from a living beldon, like shearing. There is no other source of it on the planet — the Empire's own station exists to meter this.

label: tikkarr
description: A long-legged, kelp-coloured crab-thing that lives up in the kelp forest, not on the floor — clinging, cutting, carrying fronds down to its holes. It is the sea-farm's pest and its pollinator both; cut kelp plots without tikkarr in them grow back slow. Armored, a good meal in the legs, and fond of nets.

label: tubbik
description: A Spender. A pea-sized gas-bladder animal that exists for the flood-weeks and nothing else: the first rise lifts a billion of them out of the clay, they feed, they breed, they die, and the carpet of them on the falling water is what the fliers commute in for. Between floods the water holds only stragglers. Cooked in a mass it is a paste; the Farmers call it flood-bread and are not joking.

label: tuun
description: The water's Swinger. A small, quick, bark-mottled octopus that climbs the root causeways out of the water to reach the fruit-fall, and has been seen on the lower boughs. It steals. Lines, bait, small bright things, a fisher's whole catch left on the bank. Rare on the hook because it is usually the one holding the hook. Good eating, if you can find it.

label: ullo
description: A soft bell the size of two cupped hands, near-invisible by day, that lights a slow blue pulse from dusk. Ullo rise together and drift as a lit crowd while the fan-dancers display on the bank; the pools are places of romance and the ullo have never been told otherwise. Netted, it is a sting and a disappointment -- mostly water, a little meat, and the light goes out in your hands.

label: uvva
description: A bladder-bodied grazer that hangs under the surface with its mouth open, waiting for the fruit-fall. When a giant drops its crop the uvva rise in a crowd and gorge -- and the fruit's accelerants work on them as on everything, so a fed uvva bloats, spins slowly, passes seed downstream and starts again. The river's seed-carrier. Sweet, faintly fizzy, and it does the same to you.

label: vhessa
description: A Patient one, and the reason the canyon water has no truce. A pale slot-canyon squid that hangs in the roofed water with its arms laid flat along the rock wall like roots, invisible, and takes what comes down to drink. It has no need to hurry. Landed, it is mostly arm, and the arms keep working for a while. The Farmers say you have not caught one — it has let go of the wall to see what you are.

label: visceral meat
description: Dense insectoid meat off a visceral, the biome's sealed-horror predator. It carries the same bio-accumulated metal load every other carcass here does, cooked out just enough to be a delicacy instead of a coroner's report.

label: vobbal
description: Eight soft arms and a bulb of a body, living in the hollows where the seep water enters the pool. It takes things. Pebbles, offerings, a dropped tool, a ring -- and it stacks them, carefully, in towers in the shallows, and knocks them down, and stacks them again. Some oases forbid catching them; most simply don't. The ones who do eat them say it is very good, in a voice that suggests they would ra

label: zeev
description: A hand-long river squid, green-gold, that lives in the fast clean reaches and moves the way the river does -- one hard pulse and gone. Shoals of them ride the current down through the root causeways and pulse back up at night. Fast to catch, faster to spoil; the Wildsteam eat them off the line. Its ink is nothing special. Its cousin's is.

label: zhiil
description: The young of the thing that makes the V-wake. Hand-long, black, ridged, a body built of the same propane-native chemistry as its parent and already agitated by anything that moves in the fuel — a zhiil in a net thrashes until it freezes solid, and then it is a spiny black icicle that thaws back to thrashing on the fire. Scrapers who have fished up a zhiil pull the line and leave, because the paren

Water wakes it; it rises through the softened clay into the canyon pools, feeds, breeds, and seals itself down again before the pan cracks. Its shed cell-lining is the crack-wax the Farmers trade.
